papers.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
papers.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. Under chronic hypers
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant genes in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture coordinating antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages, providing a framework for understanding salinity tolerance in this xerohalophyte.

papers.title: An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To characterize systemic transcriptomic signatures and identify candidate hub genes associated with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) in peripheral blood using an integrative systems-biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies an integrative systems-biology approach to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene-expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets for LSCC. The work is exploratory and relies on computational network analysis rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating how accurately the resulting network structures capture causal gene-gene relationships. This addresses a gap in widely available software for both Bayesian network inference and structural causal assessment in single-cell GRN analysis.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that aligns consecutive tissue sections from spatial multi-omics experiments using only their associated images, without requiring shared molecular features or prior annotations. It enables the creation of unified multi-modal molecular datasets by physically aligning slides from different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions, achieving performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools.

papers.title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.
papers.abstract: Gravitropism redirects plant organ growth by converting gravity perception into asymmetric growth initiated in endodermal statocytes. Although the C2H2-type zinc finger transcription factor SHOOT GRAVITROPISM 5 (SGR5), also known as INDETERMINATE DOMAIN 15 (IDD15), is essential for shoot gravitropism, the transcriptional mechanisms linking gravity perception to directional growth remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing to build a transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis inflorescence stem, revealing the endodermal gene regulatory network that controls gravitropism. The authors identify how the transcription factor SGR5/IDD15 links gravity perception in endodermal statocytes to asymmetric growth, providing a transcriptional framework for this process.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in data integration: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.
papers.abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of
papers.summary: This perspective paper proposes 'Longevitomics' as a unified systems-science framework for studying healthy longevity, arguing that its determinants are currently fragmented across separate molecular layers (genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome, digital phenotyping, AI). It defines the 'Longevitome' as the dynamic, integrated architecture of these multi-omic and phenotypic layers underlying long life. The contribution is conceptual rather than empirical, aiming to organize longevity research around an integrative modeling approach.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira cultured at host-like 37°C upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that these bacteria rely mainly on long-chain fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
papers.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from lab to field for soil bioremediation by integrating mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives. It identifies key barriers limiting field performance and proposes evidence-based design principles for engineering plant-microbe-soil consortia.

papers.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.
papers.summary: scPhyloGRN is a new computational method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by explicitly incorporating the lineage tree (phylogeny) of individual cells. By using cellular ancestry to distinguish expression variation driven by shared lineage from that driven by cell state, the method aims to produce more accurate gene-level regulatory relationships. The work addresses a key confounder in single-cell GRN inference, where both developmental history and current cell state shape expression patterns.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.
papers.summary: This paper presents a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging cochlea, tracking how individual cell types change across the lifespan. It identifies two distinct phases of age-related inflammation (biphasic inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network reconstruction, and bulk cross-cohort validation into a single temporal framework.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relate to semen quality in rams, using ejaculates from five animals assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis. The authors report an association between protamine gene expression and sperm motility, and use gene regulatory network analysis to propose upstream regulators. The work extends protamine biology from well-studied species into ram reproduction, though the small sample size limits generalization.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted meta-classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weights vary edge by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology characterizing why methods disagree on individual edges. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the work reframes inter-method disagreement as a signal to be exploited rather than a nuisance to be averaged away.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors report a high-quality genome annotation (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and identify 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEAs whose coordinated regulation may underlie salt tolerance. The work provides a genomic and regulatory resource for understanding environmental resilience in this halophyte.

papers.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell multiomics data to map the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis, revealing cellular and molecular changes underlying disease pathogenesis. The findings provide a comprehensive atlas of cell-cell communication in AR, highlighting key epithelial-stromal interactions that may drive chronic inflammation.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.
papers.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold tremendous promise for disease modeling, drug discovery, and cardiac regenerative therapies. However, the immature phenotype of hPSC-CMs remains a major barrier limiting their translational utility. Here, we performed integrated multi-omic profiling to identify molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with hPSC-CM maturation during long-term culture. hPSC-CMs were cultured for 113 days and analyzed using metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics across progressive stages of maturation. Long-term culture induced
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) over 113 days of culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs that drive maturation. Long-term culture induced progressive maturation-associated changes across multiple molecular layers. The work provides a multi-omic resource for understanding and potentially improving hPSC-CM maturation, a key barrier to their translational use in disease modeling and cardiac therapy.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review argues that the TREM2 receptor acts as a central regulator of macrophage behavior in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the simple M1/M2 classification toward a more nuanced view of macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity. It emphasizes that the timing of TREM2 signaling matters and highlights TREM2 as a potential therapeutic target, though the abstract describes a conceptual synthesis rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This paper argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch/Dale and Bradford Hill are insufficient for toxicology in networked biological systems such as AOP networks and multi-omics data, where mechanisms are multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions and quantitative methods—to guide causal inference in these complex settings. The work is a conceptual and methodological review aimed at improving how toxicologists assess causation in networked systems.

papers.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal temporal tra
papers.summary: This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis reveals temporal regulatory transitions underlying injury and regeneration, and identifies candidate renoprotective factors. The work provides a dynamic molecular map of cisplatin nephrotoxicity that could inform protective strategies.

papers.title: Neutrophil-microglia communication through the C3-C3aR1 axis contributes to secondary neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a rapidly evolving neuroinflammatory response that contributes to secondary brain injury. Although infiltrating leukocytes and resident microglia are both prominent components of this response, the cellular signals that connect peripheral immune-cell recruitment to microglial state remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates how peripheral immune cells and resident microglia communicate after traumatic brain injury to drive secondary neuroinflammation. The authors identify the complement C3-C3aR1 signaling axis as a key mediator of neutrophil-microglia crosstalk, linking infiltrating leukocyte recruitment to changes in microglial state.

papers.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning m
papers.summary: This review argues that computational predictions of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities are often conflated with experimentally validated ones, and that this distinction should be the starting point for AI-driven precision oncology. It surveys how machine learning and genome-scale systems biology generate metabolic hypotheses at scale, and discusses what is needed to bridge the gap between predicted and confirmed synthetic lethal targets.

papers.title: ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models.
papers.abstract: Air pollution is one of the leading global environmental health risks, associated with millions of premature deaths annually. It represents a substantial share of the global disease burden. Despite well-established epidemiological associations, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain only partially understood. There is a need for systematic approaches toward mechanistic understanding that connect particulate matter exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects.
papers.summary: This paper presents ExposomeMap-PM, a framework that maps fine and ultrafine particulate matter exposure to molecular mechanisms using adverse outcome pathways and systems biomedicine disease models. It aims to systematically connect air pollution exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects, addressing the gap between epidemiological associations and mechanistic understanding.

papers.title: Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated outcomes diverge across individuals with similar genetic backgrounds and environmental exposures, reflecting trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, and partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints. Despite advances in systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling, translating this complexity into clinically actionable reasoning remains difficult: these disciplines generate increasingly detailed representations of immune behavior that deepen mechanistic understanding while raising barriers to integration across clinica
papers.summary: This perspective proposes the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework to explain why individuals with similar genetic and environmental backgrounds develop divergent immune-mediated phenotypes. The framework conceptualizes immune outcomes as trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent state space defined by activation, constraint, and tissue context, rather than fixed molecular endpoints. It aims to bridge systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling with clinically actionable reasoning.
